rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Full sequential read of chunks 0-13: every pronoun/demonstrative resolves either in-chunk or against a term this file itself already named ("the three lenses" earned at chunk 3 L15, reused chunks 4/8; "the artefact" earned chunk 4 L23, reused chunk 6/8; "the packaged session/re-send" earned across chunks 0/3, reused chunks 8-13). Closest-to-violating: chunk 8 L74-75 "the kit" ("which failure the kit caught", "before you credit the kit") is a synonym never literally introduced as "kit" before — but "packaged"/"packaging" is the file's H1-title-level running metaphor (chunk 3 L16 "the packaging that catches it", chunk 0 title "re-send packaged", chunk 8 L72 "the packaged session"), so a reader arriving at chunk 8 with full prior context resolves "kit" to "the packaging" without ambiguity; stays inside. Second closest: chunk 3 L17 "Ralph re-feed" is named with zero in-file explanation (its only expansion lives in M6's `agents-that-build-agents.md`, confirmed absent from any M5 file) and chunk 10 L98 only names its origin, not its mechanism — but per rule 1's own text this is a naming-before-earning question ("Premature use still fails check_writing.md §14... that's a writing-class flag, not a slides one"), not a referent-resolution failure: "Ralph re-feed" is introduced as one item in a 3-item menu alongside two other undefined-in-this-file terms ("LLM judge", "shell-hook"), not referred back to as already known.

grep for opening-lecture/earlier-module/positional-callback phrasing across the body returns one candidate: chunk 4 L23 "the lecture ahead hands you the lenses to read it with." This is a forward, sequential ("ahead" = deck-order, not page-geometry) navigational pointer to the module's own linked lecture (`reading-the-return.md`, linked two chunks later at L37) -- it does not claim to already contain that lecture's content, so it isn't a narrative callback pretending delivery; it's the module's own signposting, which rule 1's carve-out explicitly treats as prior context the file's own includes may draw on. No instance of naming another file's content by position ("the opening lecture said...") found.

All 14 chunks carry a self-standing claim or substantive bulleted content (verified individually against the chunk map above) -- none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Shortest chunks (12 "Pre-reads", 13 "Next") each still carry one complete, self-contained statement.

Checked every non-canonical (claim-shaped) header against its own chunk content: chunk 5 "Say what done-done means" delivers exactly that (a done-done prompt); chunk 6 "Your mid-run worries hint at missing checks" delivers worry-to-check content; chunk 8 "Inspect your results" delivers a critical read of the return; chunk 9 "Back to the map, one last time" delivers the map-figure revisit. No header is contradicted by its content. Closest-to-notable: chunk 13 "## Next" (L117-120) is now one sentence ("Module 6 reads the packaged session: subtler misses, subtler drift") rather than the compendium's usual two-sentence "what M6 does / what the student carries" shape -- git diff shows this was Antti's own 2026-09-02/03 edit (commit "M5 stops promising an M6 that no longer answers who reviewed what") cutting a since-stale claim. The dropped clause is not restored because chunk 11 "## Bring to Module 6" (immediately above) already states what the student carries -- re-adding it in "## Next" would be the doctrine-restatement rule 16(a) forbids. Header still self-carries the content actually present; stays inside.
